385:
(a) Program established. There is established in the city a permit parking program whereby motor vehicles bearing a special parking permit issued pursuant to this code section may be parked on streets or within certain areas known as permit parking areas. For the purposes of this code section, the following streets areas are designated as permitted parking only:
(1) Ridley Avenue between Smith Street and Mitchell Avenue;
(2) W. Bacon Street between New Franklin Road and Marshall Street; and
(3) Highland Avenue between Ridley Avenue and N. Greenwood Street.
(b) Application for permit. The application for a parking permit shall provide the following information:
(1) The name of the operator of the motor vehicle to be permitted;
(2) The operator's residential address;
(3) The operator's state driver's license number;
(4) The motor vehicle make, model and license number; and
(5) Any other information reasonably requested on the application form. The applicant shall also provide proof of residency within the designated permitted parking area.
(c) Permit term; fee. Annual parking permits shall be valid for the calendar year of issuance, will expire on December 31st of each year, and shall be issued free of charge.
(d) Issuance of permits. The department of community development shall issue parking permits as follows: A permit shall be issued only to a motor vehicle operator who resides or operates a business on property that is located within the designated permit parking area, which permit shall be issued in accordance with the following limitations:
(1) For single-family dwelling units (one residential structure containing only one housing unit) or commercial uses:
One parking permit may be issued for each valid street address where said dwelling unit or commercial use contains off-street parking.
(2) For multiple family dwelling units (including but not limited to, apartments, condominiums, attached dwellings, row houses and townhouses):
One parking permit may be issued for each legally constituted and existing dwelling unit in any two-family or multiple-family dwelling facility at a valid street address within the permit parking area where said dwelling unit contains off-street parking availability.
(3) Additional parking permits may be issued, for good and sufficient cause, to any resident or business operator within the permit parking area if, in the opinion of the LaGrange Police Department, exceptional circumstances exist warranting an additional permit issuance.
(e) Permit form and display.
(1) The parking permit shall be a hang tag type and shall be displayed only on the motor vehicle for which it was issued in accordance with the limitations of use. The permit shall be prominently displayed by hanging from the rear view mirror so that is clearly visible from outside the vehicle. Information shown on the permit shall include the expiration date.
(2) Visitors to a residence within the permitted parking area may utilize the registered owner's parking permit while visiting said residence.
(f) The department of community development office may issue a temporary parking permit, valid for not more than one year, for a vehicle operated by a person who provides health care services on a regular basis at an address within a permit parking area. Such temporary permit shall be a permit bearing special validation and may be issued upon satisfactory proof of need presented by the resident at such address.
(g) Limitations of use. A motor vehicle which displays a valid parking permit shall be allowed to stand or park in the parking permit area for which the permit has been issued. Such permits shall not authorize a motor vehicle to stand or park in any place where or during any time when the stopping, standing or parking of a motor vehicle is otherwise prohibited or the area is designated for other uses.
(h) Signage. Signs will be erected in each permitted parking area indicating that the street is designated as permitted parking only and that parking is prohibited without a permit.
(i) Penalties for violations.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to stand or park any motor vehicle on any street within the permitted parking area which does not display a valid parking permit. However, a public utility vehicle or commercial vehicle which is actively engaged in utility work or delivery or picking up of items is exempt from obtaining a permit and will not be in violation of this section.
(2) It shall be unlawful and a violation of this code section for a person to furnish false information in an application for any permit authorized by this section or to represent falsely that such person is eligible for such permit.
(3) A person holding a valid parking permit issued pursuant to this code section shall not be allowed the use or display of such permit on a vehicle other than that for which the permit was issued or a visitor to his/her residence or business.
(4) It shall be unlawful and a violation of this code section for a person to produce or display a facsimile or counterfeit parking permit in order to evade the limitations on parking in a permit parking area.
(5) Violation of this section shall constitute an offense and shall be punishable as provided under Code section 1-1-6. In addition to said penalty, a vehicle found to be in violation of this code section is subject to immediate removal, at the owner's expense, by a law enforcement officer.
(Ord. No. 16-01, § 1, 3-22-16)

394:
The city uses a block towing system when there exists the need for services of a wrecker or tow truck as a result of a motor vehicle accident or collision on a street or road within the city. The block towing system is reserved for those instances in which the person in need of the wrecker or tow truck service does not elect to use a specific wrecker or tow truck operator. In such instances, the city, by and through the chief of police or his designee, shall establish and administer a rotating list as more particular described herein. Block towing ends when the customer requests and the wrecker or tow truck operator agrees to delivery of a vehicle to a site other than one of the tow company's designated impound/storage sites.
(Ord. No. 25-07, § 2, 2-11-25)
395:

If the service is a corporation, the names and addresses of its officers and any stockholders owning twenty percent (20%) or more of the corporate stock must be included. If the service is a partnership, the names of all partners must be included.
(2) Complete list of towing equipment, including the VIN for motor vehicles, noting thereon any wreckers which are rated to tow tractor trailers.

For purposes of corporations, the application shall include similar information as to any officers or stockholders holding twenty percent (20%) or more of the corporate stock. If the applicant is a partnership, said application shall include similar information as to all partners.

One hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) bodily injury to any one person;
Three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000.00) bodily injury to two or more person;
Fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) property damage; and
Fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) garage keepers legal liability (GKLL) insurance.

It is declared to be the intent of the governing authority of the city, in furtherance of its responsibility to protect the public health, safety and welfare of its citizens, to enact the following regulations governing the maintenance of property and the removal of hazards therefrom, all in order to assure the prevention and abatement of nuisances.

404:
Except as specifically defined in this section, all words used in this chapter have their customary dictionary definitions. Unless otherwise expressly stated, the following words shall have the meaning herein indicated:
Ashes shall mean the residue from the burning of wood, coal or other combustible material.
Breeding places shall mean a mound or mass of construction debris, garbage, trash, cut vegetation or woody material.
Buffer shall mean a ten-foot wide strip of land maintained in such a manner that the growth of vegetation does not interfere with the property of another or exceed twelve (12) inches in height.
Developed property shall mean property upon which a structure has been erected which requires permanent location on the ground or which is attached to something having permanent location on the ground.
Filth shall mean foul, rotten or putrid matter which causes offensive odors and creates unhealthy conditions.
Garbage shall mean putrescible animal and vegetable waste resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking and consumption of food.
Inoperable vehicle shall mean any vehicle that is resting on blocks, without tires, with major parts missing, in a state of repair which precludes use, or lacking required current registration certificate.
Litter shall mean any kind of discarded and uncontrolled or uncontained solid waste, garbage, trash, dirt, sand, gravel, refuse, debris, dead animal or thing or substance, whether liquid or solid, that may be carried or deposited, in whole or in part, by wind, rain, snow, water, animal or any other such force into any public or private property, or into any river, public waterway, drain, sewer or receiving basin.
Livestock means all animals of the equine, bovine or swine class, including goats, sheep, mules, horses, hogs, cattle, and other grazing animals, and all rarities, including, but not limited to, ostriches, emus and rheas.
Person shall mean firms, partnerships, associations, organizations, trusts, companies and bodies, politic and corporate, or any other group of individuals acting as a unit, or any combination thereof, as well as individuals.
Poultry shall mean domestic fowl, including, but not limited to, water fowl such as geese and duck, birds which are bred for meat and egg production, exhibition, or competition; game birds such as pheasants, partridge, quail and grouse, as well as guinea fowl, pigeons, dove, peafowl; and all other avian species.
Private property shall mean property privately owned by one (1) or more persons.
Public property shall mean any street, alley, sidewalk or other public thoroughfare in the city or property owned and controlled by any governmental entity.
Refuse shall mean all putrescible or nonputrescible waste (except body waste) including, but not limited to, garbage, rubbish, ashes, street cleanings, dead animals, abandoned automobiles, equipment, appliances, machinery, and solid market and industrial waste.
Rubbish shall mean nonputrescible waste (excluding ashes) consisting of both combustible and noncombustible waste, including, but not limited to, paper, cardboard, cans, yard clippings, wood, woody tree cuttings, glass, bedding, crockery and similar materials.
Running at large shall mean any livestock which is not under manual control of a person and which is on any public road of the city or any property not belonging to the owner of the livestock, unless by permission of the owner of such property.
Street shall mean the entire width between boundary lines of every right-of-way publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular or pedestrian travel.
Trash shall mean organic and inorganic waste that is too large or heavy to be routinely broken down, compressed, or otherwise disassembled to fit into the normal solid waste containers authorized for use by a household or business for the collection of its waste. Trash includes, but is not limited to, items such as lumber, bedding, furniture and garden tools, but does not include yard trimmings.
Undeveloped property shall mean property that does not have upon it anything constructed or erected which requires permanent location on the ground or which is attached to something having a permanent location on the ground.
Vegetation shall mean grass, weeds, or plants having no permanent woody stem less than one (1) inch in diameter at breast height and showing no visible signs of having been maintained, as distinguished from a tree or shrub.
(Ord. No. 97-4, § 2, 1-14-97)

423:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to create a nuisance on his premises or premises occupied by him, or to permit a nuisance to remain six (6) hours after notice. The following, among others, are declared to be nuisances: Stagnant water, decayed vegetables, decayed fruits and fruit refuse, dead animals or tainted meat, filthy privies, filthy water or excrement, broken or ruptured sewer lines, raw sewage or anything that causes offensive odors or that works hurt, damage or inconvenience to another; the conducting by pipes, sewers or otherwise into any street, public alley or on the lot of another, of any filthy water or excrement of any kind, such as comes from kitchens, bathtubs, laundry places, privies, stables and other places.

If the thing complained of is a nuisance, the order shall specify within what time it is to be abated by the defendant. If it is not abated within the time specified in the order, the court shall issue a writ directed to the chief of police directing and requiring the abatement of the nuisance.
(e) Whenever the person creating or maintaining any nuisance within the city shall fail to abate after notice to do so, and it shall become necessary to issue a writ, directed to the chief of police, requiring him to remove same, it shall be the duty of the chief of police to keep an account of the necessary expenses incurred and to render to the court a statement of same. The court shall issue an execution against such order for such amount, the same to be levied upon and collected in the same manner as is provided for the levy in collection of executions for taxes.
(Ord. No. 97-4, § 2, 1-14-97)

Adequate shelter means a protective covering for a domestic animal that provides adequate space and protection to maintain the animal in a state of good health, and that prevents pain, suffering, or significant risk to the animal's health. Adequate shelter shall consist of a completely enclosed structure with four (4) sides, a constructed floor, and a roof with a door opening. It should also be clean, dry and compatible with current weather conditions, in addition to age, size, species and condition of the animal. The structure should be of sufficient size to allow the animal to stand, turn around, lie down and go in and out of the structure comfortably. To be adequate, some type of bedding that is quick drying must be provided to maintain comfortable temperatures within the structure during the months of November through March. In addition, the structure shall include a heavy plastic or rubber flap to cover the door and window openings during the months of November through March. From April through November, the structure shall either be shaded or moved out of direct sunlight. If the shelter is made of wood, it shall be raised at least two (2) inches off the ground to prevent seepage or rotting. Examples of inadequate shelter include, but are not limited to, lean-tos, metal or plastic drums, boxes, abandoned vehicles, porches, decks, or material that does not provide sufficient protection from the elements.
Livestock means all animals of the equine, bovine or swine class, including goats, sheep, mules, horses, hogs and cattle, and other grazing animals.
Owner means any person, association, firm or corporation, natural or artificial, owning, having custody of or in charge of livestock.
Running at large means any livestock which is not under manual control of a person and which is on any public road of this city or on any property not belonging to the owner of the livestock, unless by permission of the owner of such property.

(a) Permitted animals. Only the following animals may be utilized for prescribed grazing within the city; Katahdin sheep and either Boer, Kiko, Savanna or Spanish breeds of goat.
(b) Stocking rate limit. Stocking rate refers to the total number of grazing animals permitted on a property. There shall be no more than one (1) prescribed grazing animal per five hundred (500) square feet of lot size at any time. Animals less than six (6) months of age that accompany an adult female animal of the same species shall not be included in stocking rate calculations. Any stocking rate calculation that results in a fractional unit amount shall be rounded up to the next whole number portion of the calculation to determine the number of allowable prescribed grazing animals allowed on site.
(c) Duration. Prescribed grazing shall not be permitted for more than five (5) consecutive days at a time on a property. No more than four (4) permits for prescribed grazing may be issued per calendar year per parcel. There shall be a minimum of thirty (30) consecutive days between the expiration of one permit and the issuance of the next.
(d) Proper enclosure. The prescribed grazing activity shall be fully and properly enclosed at all times. Proper enclosure refers to any combination of temporary or permanent fences or structures designed to prevent the escape of the prescribed grazing animals and to protect the prescribed grazing animals from the intrusion of other animals. All sides of the enclosure(s) shall be of sufficient height and the bottom of the enclosures shall be constructed or secured in a manner as to prevent prescribed grazing animals from escaping over or under the enclosure(s).
(1) Permanent fences and structures shall comply with the regulations for the zoning district in which the prescribed grazing is located and shall be permitted separately from the prescribed grazing activity.
(2) Temporary fencing and structures for the sole purpose of enclosing prescribed grazing animals shall comply with the regulations for the zoning districts in which the prescribed grazing is located, and can be permitted in association with the prescribed grazing activity. Temporary fences may be electric or electrified and are exempted from landscape buffering requirements as required in certain zoning districts.
(Ord. No. 22-09, § 1, 5-24-22)

556:
It is declared to be the intent of the city, in furtherance of its responsibility to protect the public health, safety and well-being of its citizens to protect and enhance the quality of its environment by enacting policies governing the storage, collection, transportation and disposal of solid waste, as that term is hereinafter defined in this chapter, in accordance with the comprehensive state-wide program for solid waste management now in effect in the State of Georgia. 557:
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them:
Ashes: The residue from the burning of wood, coal, coke or other combustible material.
Biomedical waste: Any solid waste which contains medical residue, pathological waste, biological waste, cultures, and stocks of infectious agents and associated biologicals, contaminated animal carcasses (body parts, their bedding and other wastes from such animals), chemotherapy waste, discarded medical equipment and parts as now or hereafter defined in the Rules of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources Environmental Protection Division.
City: The City of LaGrange, Georgia.
Collector: The person or persons as defined herein who, under agreements, verbal or written, with or without compensation does the work of collecting and/or transporting solid wastes, provided however, that this definition shall not include an individual collecting and/or transporting waste from his own single-family dwelling unit.
Commercial solid waste: All types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses, and other nonmanufacturing activities, excluding residential and industrial wastes. This includes landscaping companies who generate yard trimmings and other solid waste by the establishment and maintenance of landscaping on residential properties and waste generated from an operation conducted from a residence requiring a business license.
Commercial hauler: A person, firm or corporation engaged in the business of solid waste collection and/or hauling in the city as a service and for which a fee is charged and received and which is licensed for that purpose by the city.
Composting: The controlled biological decomposition of organic matter into a stable, odor-free humus.
Construction/demolition waste: Waste building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair and demolition operations on pavements, houses, commercial buildings or other structures. Such wastes include, but are not limited to asbestos-containing waste, wood, bricks, metal, concrete, wallboard, paper, cardboard, inert waste landfill material and other nonputrescible wastes.
Container: A receptacle designed for the temporary reception and storage of solid waste pending transportation to a municipal solid waste landfill or other licensed solid waste landfill or transfer station.
Garbage: Any putrescible or nonputrescible, organic or inorganic, combustible or noncombustible wastes, wastes from the preparation, cooking and serving of foods or liquids, market wastes, wastes from the handling and storage of produce, and those items of solid waste normally generated within a residential household which can be properly and safely fitted into an approved solid waste container.
Hazardous waste: Any solid waste which is, has been or in the future may be, defined as a hazardous substance by federal, state or local law, or which has hazardous constituent of sufficient quantity as defined in regulations promulgated by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources in Chapter 391-3-11 of the Official Compilation of Rules and Regulations of the State of Georgia.
Industrial waste: Solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes that is not a hazardous waste regulated under the Hazardous Waste Management Act and regulations promulgated by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources in Chapter 391-3-Il of the Official Compilation of Rules and Regulations of the State of Georgia.
Inert waste: Wastes that will not or are not likely to cause production of leachate of environmental concern. Such wastes are limited to earth and earth-like products, concrete, cured asphalt, rock, bricks, yard trash, stumps, limbs and leaves.
Litter: Any kind of discarded and uncontrolled or uncontained solid waste, garbage, trash, dirt, sand, gravel, refuse, debris, dead animal or thing or substance whatsoever, whether liquid or solid, that may be carried or deposited, in whole or in part, by the wind, rain, snow, water, animal, or any other such force into any public or private property, or into and river, public waterway, drain, sewer or receiving basin.
Liquid waste: Any waste material that is determined to contain "free liquids" as defined by Method 9095 (Paint Filter Liquids Test), and as described in "Test Methods for the Evaluation of Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
Mulching: Chipping, grinding or shredding organic materials, limbs, trees, stumps, yard trimmings and the like into small pieces for the purpose of reuse as landscape bedding, volume reduction prior to final disposal or further processing such as composting.
Municipal solid waste: Any solid waste derived from households, including garbage, trash and sanitary waste in septic tanks and means solid waste from single-family and multifamily residences, hotels and motels, bunkhouses, campgrounds, picnic grounds and day use recreational areas. The term includes yard trimmings and commercial solid waste, but does not include solid waste from mining, agricultural or silvicultural operations or industrial processes or operations.
Municipal solid waste landfill (MSWL): A disposal facility in which any amount of municipal solid waste, whether or not mixed with or including commercial waste, industrial waste or nonhazardous sludges is disposed of under controlled circumstances and by means of placing an acceptable or approved cover thereon.
Open dump: An area at which solid waste from one (1) or more sources is left to decompose, burn or which otherwise creates a nuisance or a threat to human health or the environment.
Putrescible waste: Waste that is capable of being decomposed by micro organisms, capable of generating noxious or offensive gases or odors, or which during or after decay may serve as breeding areas or feeding material for insects or animals.
Recoverable material: A material which has a known use, reuse or recycling potential and which can be feasibly used, reused or recycled.
Scavenging: The salvaging of or rummaging through the garbage, trash, disposed products or, solid waste of another by any person, who is not authorized or licensed by the city to pick up and remove the waste, without the consent of the owner or generator of the waste.
Sharps: Any discarded articles that may cause punctures or cuts, including but not limited to needles, intravenous tubing, needles, syringes or scalpel blades.
Solid waste: Any putrescible or nonputrescible waste or discarded material including solid, liquid, semisolid, or contained gaseous material resulting from residential, industrial, commercial, mining, and agricultural operations and from community activities, but does not include recovered materials.
Special waste: Those wastes requiring specific processing, handling or disposal techniques as determined necessary by the city manager or his designee which are different from the techniques normally utilized for handling or disposal. Examples of such waste types may include, but are not limited to: Mining waste; fly ash; bottom ash; sludges; friable asbestos; industrial waste; large dead animals or large quantities of dead animals and residue; foundry waste; petroleum contaminated wastes; municipal solid waste ash; or contaminated soil from the cleanup of a spill.
Trash: Organic and inorganic waste that is too large or heavy to be routinely broken down, compressed or otherwise disassembled to fit into the normal solid waste containers authorized for use by a household or business for the collection of its waste. Trash includes, but is not limited to items such as lumber, bedding, furniture, garden tools, etc., but does not include yard trimmings.
Unauthorized accumulation: An unauthorized accumulation of solid waste or litter is any amount of either which is not contained or packaged as required by this article and which is stored or allowed to accumulate on any premises in the city in a manner that may create unsanitary conditions, fire hazards, cause offensive and obnoxious odors, provide a breeding place for insects or a harboring place for vermin, invite plundering, endanger the safety of children or adults, reduce property values or in any way or manner affect adversely the health, safety, welfare and well-being of the public.
Yard trimmings: The organic material generated from maintenance by an owner or occupant of improved ground areas. Trimmings may include leaves, brush, clippings, shrub and tree prunings and discarded Christmas trees, but does not include grass clippings.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 96-32, § 1, 5-14-96; Ord. No. 02-19, § 1, 5-28-02; Ord. No. 20-24, § 8, 11-24-20)
558:

(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96)
568:
In order to protect the public health and sanitation, all improved residential properties within the city shall receive regular garbage and trash collection services from the city sanitation division. No owner of an improved residential property shall be exempt or relieved from payment of the monthly collection fee by reason of failure or refusal of such owner or his tenant or tenants, to accept collection and handling services as provided by the city sanitation division.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96)
569:
The director of public services (or designee) shall provide a schedule to each residence receiving garbage collection service from the city which shall indicate the day on which collection will be made.

570:
All residential solid waste stored outside the residence pending collection shall be placed inside approved containers with lids tightly affixed. Approved containers shall be those issued by the city to residential customers pursuant to this article, designed to be rolled to curbside for periodic collection. Under no circumstances will garbage outside of city-issued containers be collected. If necessary, extra containers may be obtained for an additional monthly fee. Each container shall bear a serial number and shall be registered to the assigned customer. All containers shall remain the property of the city. For residential customers opting to receive "premium" service (see section 15-10-24) or mobility-impaired residents, all solid waste must be placed in the city-provided containers. All recyclable items should be taken to a drop-off center. Except when taken to the curbside for scheduled collection, containers shall be located near the residence and outside of fenced enclosures in which animals are kept. Containers shall be used exclusively for the storage and transport of solid waste to the curbside.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 02-24, § 1, 8-27-02; Ord. No. 24-16, § 2, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
571:
Three (3) levels of service for the collection of residential solid waste are provided by the city:
(1) Curbside garbage collection: By 6:30 a.m. on the scheduled day for collection, customers place their container on the street shoulder in front of their residence. Containers should be placed approximately four (4) feet from the edge of the roadway, but not so as to pose a physical or visual obstruction to motorists. Where there is insufficient right-of-way adjacent to the roadway, or other topographical difficulties exist which make it unreasonable to conform to the general requirements, customers should place their container at a location mutually agreeable to the customer and sanitation department, after consultation with the director of public services (or designee). All containers shall be removed from the curbside and returned to the customer's residence no later than 8:00 a.m. on the day following the day of service.
(2) Assisted service for households with mobility-impaired residents: Households in which all regular residents are mobility-impaired may apply for assisted collection service at the same fee as levied for curbside collection. City personnel will enter upon the customer's property to collect their solid waste from city-issued container(s) on the scheduled day of collection.
(3) Premium service: City personnel will enter upon a customer's property to collect their solid waste from city-issued container(s) on the scheduled day of collection if the customer subscribes to this service level.
For households subscribing to "premium" service or for those households with mobility-impaired residents, the city-issued container(s) shall be placed so that the collector shall not be required to go more than twenty (20) feet beyond the edge of the driveway, preferably visible from the street. Containers located on private property shall not be serviced until clear access is provided to both the collection vehicle and the path the collector must travel to access the container. No containers should be located within garages, carports, basements, breezeways, fenced enclosures or otherwise in the vicinity of articles not considered to be waste by the resident. Collectors shall not be required to collect solid waste from any premises where an animal perceived to be vicious is maintained without restraint. If it is not practical to place the container(s) for collection at the location above specified, the director of public services (or designee) shall designate the location of the container(s). The owner, his agent or occupant of any residential property, shall release the city from any claim of damage of any kind or nature that may result to the premises or persons located thereon, or for any other claim of damages that may result in the servicing of the residential property because of the entry upon private property.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 02-24, § 1, 8-27-02; Ord. No. 24-16, §§ 3, 4, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
572:
(a) Garbage accumulated by residents and properly placed in approved containers shall be collected once each week.
(b) Household garbage shall be drained of all liquids prior to its being placed in solid waste containers.
(c) Pet litter shall be placed in securely tied in a plastic bag not to exceed ten (10) pounds in weight and placed in the container.
(d) Disposable diapers shall be placed and tied securely in plastic bags.
(e) Packing materials such as styrofoam pellets, excelsior, etc., that can be easily scattered by the elements shall be placed in taped boxes or plastic bags.
(f) Customers are responsible for keeping containers clean and free of accumulated waste. Containers may be cleaned with a mild detergent and/or treated with an effective insecticide, if necessary, to prevent a nuisance. Bagging of all waste deposited in the city provided container will minimize the need for cleaning.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 02-24, § 1, 8-27-02; Ord. No. 21-11, § 8, 6-22-21; Ord. No. 24-16, § 5, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
573:
(a) Every owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee of a house or building used for residential, business, commercial or other purposes, is required to maintain responsibility and surveillance over the solid waste receptacles on his/her premises. For households subscribing to curbside garbage collection, it is the owner or occupants responsibility to insure that the container(s) is (are) located on the curb by 6:30 a.m. on the regularly scheduled collection day. For households subscribing to "premium" service, it is the owner or occupants responsibility to insure that the container(s) is (are) located within twenty (20) feet of the driveway by 6:30 a.m. on the regularly scheduled day of collection. City solid waste collectors shall not be responsible for picking up loose and scattered solid waste resulting from improper containerization or lack of maintenance of the generator's solid waste storage area.
(b) Any residential container provided by the city which becomes damaged, lost or stolen shall be replaced by the city and shall be paid for by the owner of the residence to which the container is assigned.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 02-24, § 1, 8-27-02; Ord. No. 24-16, § 6, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
574:
Trash and large items which are of such a nature as to prevent placement in a receptacle may be placed at the curbside or street side for collection by the city. Such solid waste shall be placed on public right-of-way and collected for disposal twice per month according to the following standards:
(1) Items shall not extend over the sidewalk so as to block pedestrian traffic or fall into or extend over the street so as to hinder vehicular traffic or make it difficult to use motor-driven sweepers.
(2) Items shall not be placed in the gutter, in any ditch or other path of storm water runoff.
(3) Items shall be placed on the right-of-way immediately adjacent to the property from which such items originated. Items shall not be placed on vacant lots, parks, across the street from the property on which such items originated or on another person's property.
(4) Items shall not be placed over stormwater catchbasins, water meters or valve boxes, underneath overhead utility lines or low tree branches, in the vicinity of utility poles and/or guy wires, trees, mailboxes, fire hydrants or steep banks that may impede the collection of the waste, increase the risk of damage to utilities by mechanized loading equipment, or otherwise compromise the safety of the collectors.
(5) Solid waste resulting from building construction remodeling and repairs such as plaster, roofing materials, insulation or other rubbish or debris will not be picked up or collected from rental properties, if caused by or generated from contractors or by the owner employing paid or otherwise compensated help. Any such materials will be picked up or collected from an owner occupied property if caused by or generated from work done by the owner-occupant without a contractor or otherwise compensated help if such material can be physically managed by city crews. Prior to removal of any such material, the city may require the owner to sign an affidavit or submit other reasonable proof that the work was done without the help of paid or otherwise compensated help. Debris resulting from such activities shall not exceed two (2) cubic yards or four hundred (400) pounds in weight.
(6) Rocks, dirt, concrete blocks or bricks are not considered trash and shall not be collected by the city.
(7) Household furniture and personal belongings of an evicted tenant, lessee or occupant will not be placed on city property or right-of-way and will not be collected by the city.
(8) Old furniture may be placed out for curbside collection, provided it is placed separately from other trash and yard trimmings.
(9) Uncontrolled and/or uncontained trash items shall be considered as litter, and the generator shall thereof be subject to the enforcement actions outlined in section 15-10-61.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 24-16, § 7, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
575:
Yard trimmings, as defined in this chapter, shall at all times be physically separated from containerized garbage and other forms of solid waste (trash and large items) placed curbside for collection. Yard trimmings shall be placed on public right-of-way in such manner as to not obstruct gutters, drains, walkways or streets and shall be collected by the city twice per month according to the following standards:
(1) Leaves and pine straw shall be placed in a separate pile from trimmings, clippings, limbs or brush.
(2) Small trees, tree trimmings, hedge clippings, shrubbery clippings, limbs, brush and similar materials shall be of a length and/or weight that is manageable by city collection personnel and/or equipment. Said trimmings and clippings shall be placed in a neat stack near the curbline that does not exceed four (4) cubic yards in size or exceed five hundred (500) pounds.
(3) No trees, logs, limbs, stumps, roots, dirt, brush or other debris resulting from tree removal, land or lot clearing, grading or landscape maintenance work done by contractors or by the owner employing any help or assistance, paid or otherwise compensated, will be picked up or collected by the city. Paid or otherwise compensated help as used herein shall include independent or licensed contractors but not those persons periodically employed as yard men. Compensation shall also be interpreted to include receiving as compensation the wood, limbs and other residue from such trimming and cutting. Any form of compensation shall place the burden of disposal directly upon the individual or contractor performing the task. Any such materials will be picked up or collected from an owner occupied property if caused by or generated from work done by the owner-occupant without a contractor or otherwise compensated help if such material can be physically managed by city crews and does not exceed four (4) cubic yards in size or exceed five hundred (500) pounds.
(4) No other trash, particularly solid objects such as rocks, glass bottles, wood, pieces of wire, steel or concrete should be mixed with or concealed under yard trimming piles.
(5) Yard trimmings shall not be collected by the city for unimproved and/or vacant lots, or multifamily rental units or commercial establishments utilizing the service of a commercial solid waste hauler.
(6) The location restrictions for placement on public right-of-way as specified in section 15-10-27 shall also apply to yard trimmings.
(7) Uncontrolled and/or uncontained yard trimmings shall be considered as litter and the generator shall therefore be subject to the enforcement actions outlined in section 15-10-61.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96; Ord. No. 24-16, § 8, 6-27-24, eff. 7-1-24)
577:
The city manager, or his or her designee, is authorized to waive the requirements for collection and disposal of yard trimmings and trash during organized community cleanup programs, to provide collection service at the time of the waiver, and is also authorized to waive the requirements of this section during the times of a natural disaster.

c. Additional ninety-six (96) gallon container(s), per additional container per month per residential unit: $13.25.

(a) The sidewalk pedestrian trash receptacles located in the downtown business district will be used for pedestrian trash and litter disposal only. 584:
Private businesses which operate in the city and provide solid waste collection and disposal services, shall comply with the following minimum requirements:
(1) Obtain a solid waste handling permit from the Director of Environmental Protection Division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, pursuant to O.C.G.A. 128-24.

592:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or cooperation, in person or by his agent, employee or servant, to cast, throw, sweep, or deposit in any manner in or upon any public way or other public place in the city or in any public waters, drain, sewer or receiving basin within the jurisdiction of the city, any kind of dirt, rubbish, garbage, trash, yard trimmings, leaves, concrete, rock, stagnant water, dead animal, solid waste article, thing or substance whatsoever, whether liquid or solid. 593:

(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96)
594:
It shall be unlawful for any person to place in or on any unoccupied or unattended automobile or other vehicle in the city or to otherwise distribute anywhere in the city any handbill, circular, pamphlet, poster, postcard or literature of any kind; provided, however, such distribution may be permitted directly to the occupants of business or private residences or to the occupants of occupied vehicles in such manner as not to create a litter problem.

walls and sidewalks shall be kept free of litter. Parking lots of all businesses, commercial and industrial occupancies shall be kept free of litter.
(Ord. No. 96-11, § 1, 2-27-96)
603:
(a) Litter being thrown, deposited, dropped or dumped from any motor vehicle or other means of conveyance in violation of any section of this article, shall be prima facie evidence that the operator of the conveyance has violated this article.
(b) Except as provided in subsection (a) of this section, whenever any litter which is dumped, deposited, thrown, or left on public or private property in violation of this article is discovered to contain any article, including but not limited to letters, bills, publications or other writings which display the name of a person thereon in such a manner as to indicate that the article belongs or belonged to such person, it shall be presumed that such named person is the owner of such litter and has deposited or dumped the same in violation of this article.

684:
For the purposes of this article, the following terms, phrases, words and their derivatives shall have the meaning set forth herein unless the context clearly indicates that another meaning is intended. When not inconsistent with the context, words used in the present tense include the singular, words used in the plural number include the singular number, and words used in the singular number include the plural number.
Cable services means "cable services" as defined in the Communications Act of 1934, as amended by the Cable Communications Policy Act of 1984 and the Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992, and as may be further amended from time to time (the "Cable Act"). In the event that "cable services" is no longer defined in the Cable Act or the definition in the Cable Act otherwise becomes inapplicable, "Cable Services" shall mean "cable services" as defined in the Cable Act immediately prior to such term no longer being defined in the Cable Act or such definition otherwise becoming inapplicable.
Cable system means any "cable system" as defined in the Cable Act.
City means the City of LaGrange, Georgia.
City council means the mayor and council of the city and its designee or any successor thereto.
Franchise means an initial authorization, or renewal thereof, issued by the city, whether such authorization is designated as a franchise, permit, license, resolution, contract, certificate, agreement or otherwise, which authorizes the occupation and use of the streets to provide telecommunications services.
Licensee means the holder of a valid franchise issued by the city pursuant to the provisions of this article.
May is permissive.
Ordinance means this article and all modifications and amendments thereto.
Person means any individual or any association, firm, partnership, joint venture, corporation or other legally recognized entity, whether for profit or not for profit, but shall not mean the city.
Request for proposals means the document by which the city solicits applications for franchises.
Shall is mandatory, not merely directive.
Streets means the surface of, as well as the spaces above and below, any and all streets, alleyways, avenues, highways, boulevards, driveways, bridges, tunnels, parks, parkways, public grounds or waters, and other public rights-of-way within or belonging to the city.
Telecommunications services means the receipt and/or distribution, through any means, including, without limitations, coaxial cable, optical fiber, or satellite or microwave transmission, of one (1) or more audio, voice or data signals. Telecommunications services includes both cable services and non-cable telecommunications services.
Television shall mean a system for simultaneous transmission of audio signals and transient visual images by means of electrical impulses.
(Code 1972, § 20-49; Ord. No. 94-44, § 1, 9-27-94)
State Law reference— "Cable television system" defined, O.C.G.A. § 36-18-1.

710:
No proposal for a new franchise shall be considered without payment by the applicant of application fees as provided in this section. If a franchise is granted, application fees will not be deemed a credit toward any other fees or sums due by the grantee. If an application is denied, the application fee will not be refunded.
(1) Purpose of application fees. The application fees provided by this section will serve to cover the direct and indirect costs incurred by the city in processing the application, evaluating the applicant, and granting a franchise, and shall include, but not be limited to, administrative, engineering, publication, legal, and consultant's expenses.
(2) Base application fee. Notwithstanding any other requirement of this article, each applicant must pay in advance at the time of application, the sum of two thousand dollars ($2,000.00) as a nonrefundable base application fee.
(3) Additional application fee. In addition to the base application fee, each applicant shall furnish to the city a deposit in the amount of two thousand dollars ($2,000.00) by certified check or cashier's check payable to the city. In the event the expenses incurred by the city shall exceed the base application fee, the documented amount of such excess costs shall be deemed an additional application fee and shall be deducted from the deposit. The city shall refund the balance of the additional application fee to the applicant within sixty (60) days after final action to grant or deny a franchise.
(Ord. No. 94-44, § 2, 9-27-94)

714:
(a) The city may make such investigations and take or authorize the taking of such other steps as the city council deems necessary or appropriate to consider and act on applications for franchises and determine whether a franchise should be granted to an applicant, and may require the applicant to furnish additional information and data for this purpose. In considering applications, the city council may seek advice from other city officials or bodies, from such other advisory bodies as it may establish or determine appropriate, or from the public, and may request the preparation of one (1) or more reports to be submitted to the city council, which may include recommendations with respect to such applications.
(b) If the city council, after considering such information as it determines to be appropriate, elects to further consider one (1) or more applications, the city council shall set one (1) or more public hearings for consideration of the application(s), fixing and setting forth a day, hour and place certain when and where any persons having any interest therein or objections thereto may file written comments and appear before the city council and be heard, and providing notice of such public hearing(s) in accordance with applicable law.
(c) The city council may authorize negotiations between the city officials and applicants to determine whether the city and such applicants are able to reach agreement on the terms of the proposed franchise.
(d) Upon completion of the steps deemed appropriate by the city council the city council may grant the franchise, and may specify the conditions under which the franchise is granted. Alternatively, the city may reject any and all applications from whatever source and whenever received. The city also reserves the right to waive any or all requirements when it determines that the best interest of the city may be served thereby and may, if it so desires, request new or additional proposals.
